appearance.themeHelp: Light is the first-run default. System follows the operating-system appearance and switches live when the OS appearance changes.
appearance.reducedMotionHelp: Follow system honors the operating-system reduced-motion setting. You can also force reduction on or off.
appearance.languageHelp: English is the source locale. Translations for the other accepted locales are not delivered yet, so selecting them renders English until the locale resources are reviewed.
appearance.densityWithheld: A compact density option is not offered: it renders only if target-size and accessibility checks pass, and those checks have not run.
appearance.applied: Changes apply immediately. Reset restores the documented defaults: Light theme, motion following the system, and English.

shortcuts.body: The shortcuts below are implemented in the current shell. The full shortcut registry and the remap and disable controls ship in a later package.
shortcuts.localNote: Shortcut preferences are a local per-device preference.

connections.body: Connection management — add, rename, test, re-authenticate, and switch — needs the Core connection contracts, which are not wired in this milestone, so no connection list is shown. No connection state is invented here.
connections.listIntro: Connections are Core records shown with safe display names. This page never shows tokens or endpoints with embedded credentials.
connections.listUnavailable: The connection list is unavailable: the Core connection contracts are not wired in this milestone, so no connection records can be listed. No connection state is invented here.
connections.providerIntro: This is the same provider setup step the first-run wizard uses. You can also reach it from the first-run setup on the home page. Re-running setup never resets existing state.
connections.operationsIntro: The dedicated connection flow offers add, rename, remove, test, and re-authenticate. Each operation runs only through the Core connection contracts, which are not wired in this milestone, so each control states its real availability.
connections.opAddNote: Opens the provider connection setup below — the only connection type whose setup fields are specified in this phase. Setup for other connection types needs the Core bootstrap contracts, which are not wired yet.
connections.opRenameUnavailable: Rename applies to a connection in the list. The connection list is unavailable, so there is nothing to rename yet.
connections.opRemoveUnavailable: Remove applies to a connection in the list. The connection list is unavailable, so there is nothing to remove yet. Removal is destructive and always asks for an explicit confirmation that states its scope and effects before it runs.
connections.opTestUnavailable: Test applies to a saved connection, and none can be listed yet. The provider form below offers Test connection for the entries you are currently entering.
connections.opReauthUnavailable: Re-authentication runs through the Core session contracts, which are not wired in this milestone. When the Core reports that authentication is required, the re-authenticate path appears here and in the session menu.
connections.switchIntro: Switching is a Core-mediated context change: it changes which data and permissions are available. It never moves or copies Jobs or data between Cores.
connections.firstRunBody: You can run or resume the first-run setup at any time. Re-running setup preserves your existing choices.

updates.body: Update and maintenance status is not shown: the update-status contract is not wired in this milestone. This surface never implies checkout, expiry lockout, or any maintenance behavior.

about.body: This build contains the shared shell and approved navigation. Wordmark and brand assets are deferred pending the owner's decision; the product name appears as plain text.
about.versionDisclaimer: This is the local UI shell version only. It makes no claim about the newest or most secure available release.
